title: Design Distributed Message Queue (Apache Kafka)
subtitle: High-throughput commit log, consumer groups, zero-copy network transfer, and partition replicas

stages.title: Stage 1 — In-Memory FIFO Queue Server
stages.bottleneck: Storing messages in server RAM causes data loss on crash. Single thread limits queue throughput to 10K msgs/sec.
stages.narrative:
**In-Memory Queue MVP.** Producers push items into an in-memory queue, and consumers pop items.

**Bottleneck:** Memory limits message buffering capacity. Server reboot wipes all unconsumed messages.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Partitioned Disk-Backed Commit Logs
stages.bottleneck: Sequential disk writes are fast (100MB/s), but a single disk partition cannot scale beyond 1 disk's IOPS limit.
stages.narrative: **Append-Only Commit Logs & Partitions.** Topics are split into **Partitions**. Messages are appended to sequential disk segment files with an incremental 64-bit integer **Offset**.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Consumer Groups, Offset Tracking & Metadata Coordinator
stages.bottleneck: How to allow 100 consumers to read from a topic without message duplication or processing conflicts?
stages.narrative:
**Consumer Groups & Offset Management.**
1. **Consumer Group:** Multiple workers share partition load. Each partition is consumed by exactly 1 consumer within a group.
2. **Offset Commits:** Consumers periodically record their current offset (`__consumer_offsets`), enabling instant crash recovery.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Zero-Copy OS Transfers & Partition Replicas
stages.bottleneck: Copying data from disk -> OS page cache -> user space -> socket buffer consumes CPU cycles.
stages.narrative:
**Zero-Copy Transfer & In-Sync Replicas (ISR).**
1. **Zero-Copy Optimization:** Kafka uses the `sendfile()` system call to transfer bytes directly from OS Page Cache to the NIC DMA buffer, bypassing user memory.
2. **High Availability:** Partitions replicate across Followers (ISR). If a Leader fails, a Follower is promoted in <1 second.
